A1.justification: Both PDFs present TabStruct and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. Renamed sections, relocated discussions, and renumbered results can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 13 generators on 29 main benchmark datasets, plus supplementary experiments on larger SCMs, latent confounding, causal inference, and predictor configurations.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds original comparisons and sensitivity analyses in Appendix E, including sample-size experiments and an independent-data evaluation.

M1.justification: The default CI and global-utility procedures remain unchanged. Appendix E.4 adds optional continuous global CI and discrete global utility, the latter replacing normalized predictive scores with averaged binary Wilcoxon-test outcomes. These extend the metric computation without replacing the main method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same six main SCM datasets, five additional large SCM datasets, and 23 real-world datasets. Classification, regression, latent-confounding, and causal-inference coverage already exists in v1. The new experiments vary sample sizes and evaluation procedures within retained coverage.

E2.justification: V2 newly evaluates logistic-regression C2ST against global utility and existing density metrics in Appendix E.1, Table 22. The 13-generator roster and earlier comparisons with causal-discovery and multi-table metrics remain unchanged.

E3.justification: New protocols vary full dataset sizes from 100 to 100,000, synthetic-to-reference sample ratios, and metric formulations. Appendix E.6 adds a separate train:test:independent:validation split of 3:3:3:1. Appendix D.2 also revises the stated categorical preprocessing to specify ordinal encoding for TabDiff; this documentation change does not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends validation through numerical ranking agreement, including the top five generators; synthetic-size and data-availability sensitivity; per-feature utility profiles; alternative metric formulations; and independent-data overfitting/privacy diagnostics. The earlier normalization, large-SCM, GReaT-sort, predictor-ensemble, latent-confounding, and causal-inference analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V2 introduces a Wilcoxon signed-rank test at alpha = 0.01 for the discrete global-utility variant in Appendix E.4. The existing ten-repeat setup, fixed-seed disclosure, mean-and-standard-deviation reporting, and Spearman significance reporting remain unchanged; no increase in repeated runs is stated.

E6.justification: Table 2 and all 29 per-dataset result tables retain their values. Substantial new results include global-CI correlations of 0.50 for C2ST versus 0.83 for global utility, ranking correlations of 0.95 overall and 0.92 among the top five generators, sample-size sensitivity results, and independent-data comparisons. These are additional findings under specified analyses, not improvements to the unchanged benchmark scores.

T1.justification: Appendix E.4 introduces definitions of continuous CI using average test-failure significance levels and discrete utility using averaged binary test outcomes. The original SCM assumptions, Equations (1)-(4), and Algorithms 1-2 remain unchanged. The expanded CPDAG rationale largely reuses existing arguments, and no new proof is supplied.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: a unified evaluation framework, SCM-free global utility, the released TabStruct benchmark, and a study of 13 generators on 29 datasets. Additional validation does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly distinguishes empirical correlation from formal proof in Section 4.2. New interpretations explain three patterns of per-feature utility and discuss SMOTE overfitting, TabDiff sensitivity to reduced training data, and assessing privacy relative to independent real data. These refine the retained account of structural fidelity and its practical limitations.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents inverse transformation before AutoGluon preprocessing and identifies TabCamel and TabEval as implementation dependencies. It also adds implementation-specific convergence caveats for GOGGLE and TabDDPM. Existing hyperparameter search spaces, tuning budgets, hardware specifications, and the main code-access pointer are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds references for LightGBM, CatBoost, TabCamel, TabEval, implementation resources, and healthcare or tabular-foundation-model context. Positioning relative to CauTabBench and multi-table evaluation remains substantially unchanged. The widespread conversion to author-year citations is presentational.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes the method subsections, relocates benchmark descriptions and some interpretations, and promotes the broader-impact discussion into an expanded ethics statement alongside a reproducibility statement. Local paragraph editing and citation-style changes preserve most of the original narrative and wording.

P2.justification: V2 adds a substantial per-feature visualization comprising 21 panels in Figure 7, independent-data bar-chart comparisons in Figure 9, and new correlation and sensitivity tables. Earlier displays are retained and sometimes relocated or renumbered, including v1 Figure 7 becoming v2 Figure 8. The conference template also changes typography and table placement.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens practical validation through sample-size and metric-formulation checks, per-feature diagnostics, and independent-data comparisons in Appendix E. Clearer preprocessing documentation and the explicit empirical qualification in Section 4.2 improve reproducibility and interpretation. These are useful incremental gains over v1's already extensive validation; the central benchmark results and conclusions remain unchanged.
